rich-text

Rich text.

Attribute Type Default Value Mandatory or Not Description
nodes Array/String [] No Node list or HTML string.
space String No Consecutive spaces.

Valid Values of space

Valid Value Description
ensp Half of the size of a Chinese character space.
emsp Size of a Chinese character space.
nbsp Space size based on the font.

nodes

Currently, two types of nodes are supported, which are distinguished by type: element node and text node. The default type is element node, which is an HTML node displayed in the rich text area.

Element node: type = node

Attribute Description Type Mandatory or Not Remarks
name Tag name. String Yes Supports partially trusted HTML nodes.
attrs Attribute. Object No Supports partially trusted attributes and complies with the Pascal nomenclature.
children Subnode list. Array No The structure is the same as that of nodes.

Text node: type = text

Attribute Description Type Mandatory or Not Remarks
text Text. String Yes Supports entities.

Trusted HTML Nodes and Attributes

The class and style attributes are supported globally, and the id attribute is not supported.

Sample Code

1. HTML String Rendering

<rich-text nodes="{{htmlSnippet}}" space="nbsp" />
Page({
  data: {
    htmlSnippet: '<div style="background:#eff6ff;padding:12px;border-radius:8px;"><h4 style="color:#1d4ed8;margin:0 0 6px 0;">Macle HTML RichText</h4><p style="color:#334155;font-size:13px;margin:0;">Render formatted HTML strings with <b>bold tags</b> and <span style="color:#ef4444;">colored highlights</span>.</p></div>'
  }
});
rich-text { display: block; }

2. Node Array Structure

<rich-text nodes="{{nodeArray}}" />
Page({
  data: {
    nodeArray: [{
      name: 'div',
      attrs: { class: 'custom-node-box', style: 'color:#059669;font-weight:bold;font-size:14px;' },
      children: [{ type: 'text', text: '✓ Rendered via Structured Node Array' }]
    }]
  }
});
.custom-node-box { padding: 8px; }

Bug & Tip

  1. It is not recommended to use the string type for nodes, which may deteriorate performance.
  2. Events of all nodes are shielded in the rich-text component.
  3. The attrs attribute does not support id but supports class.
  4. The name attribute is case-insensitive.
  5. If an untrusted HTML node is used, the node and all its sub-nodes is removed.
  6. If the rich-text component is used in a customized component, only the MASS style is available for class in the rich-text component.
